results.reader_title: EU SME grants may miss open-innovation leaders
results.reader_what: A study finds selected EU SME Instrument grantees displayed less demanding open innovation than unfunded high-scoring peers.
results.reader_why: Direct historical EU research/innovation funding effectiveness and programme selection system evidence.
results.reader_more: The authors construct open-innovation engagement measures and compare funded SME Instrument applicants with Seal of Excellence firms in a selected digital SME sample. They report lower engagement on difficult open-innovation dimensions among awardees, contrary to the intended policy emphasis. Sample and operationalisation limitations prevent generalising to every EU grant cohort.

deep_analysis.research_question: A study finds selected EU SME Instrument grantees displayed less demanding open innovation than unfunded high-scoring peers.
deep_analysis.main_finding: In the study sample, funded SME Instrument awardees were less engaged in challenging open-innovation activities than similarly evaluated unfunded SMEs.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Original measure of difficult open-innovation dimensions; comparative analysis of European digital-sector SME Instrument grant recipients and Seal of Excellence companies.
deep_analysis.qualification: Exploratory selected digital SME sample; observational findings cannot establish that grant funding caused lower open-innovation engagement.
